issues.description: The problem statement asks for a `public class Course` with properties `name`, `instructor`, and `ratings`, but in both template and solution these stored properties and the initializer are declared without `public`, making them `internal` by default. This can block or confuse learners if the tests (or any external consumer) try to access `Course.name`, `Course.instructor`, `Course.ratings`, or initialize `Course` from outside the `DeveloperLib` module.
issues.suggestedFix: Match the statement by making the API public: `public let name`, `public let instructor`, `public var ratings`, and `public init(name:instructor:ratings:)` (or adjust the problem statement to clarify that only the class is public and members may remain internal).

issues.description: The course rating method’s external parameter label differs across artifacts: the problem statement and template require `addRating(stars:)`, but the solution implements `addRating(rating:)`. In Swift, external labels are part of the signature, so calls like `swiftCourse.addRating(stars: 4)` (as specified) will not compile against the solution implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method to `func addRating(stars: Int)` (and use `stars` internally), or update the template and problem statement to consistently use `addRating(rating:)` and adjust any call sites accordingly.
